name: Should I replace just the bathtub or the tub and surround together?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace just the bathtub or the tub and surround together?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Replacing only the tub is usually less disruptive and may cost less, but it can leave an aged surround, mismatched finishes, or waterproofing that is difficult to verify. Replacing the tub and surround costs more and creates a better opportunity to inspect and rebuild the wet area correctly.

Context: A surround may look acceptable while its seams, backing, or wall materials have deteriorated. Keeping it can make sense when it is compatible, dry, sound, and visually acceptable.

Key factors:
- Age and condition of the surround
- Waterproofing method and evidence of leaks
- Desired finish and maintenance level
- Whether the valve, shelves, or grab bars need changes

Practical guidance: Ask the contractor to inspect the surround and explain what will be preserved, opened, or replaced. Compare the near-term savings with the possibility of paying for demolition and finish matching later.

Elite Remodeling & Design can address the tub and surrounding bathroom elements within one coordinated remodeling scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace both when the surround is damaged, outdated, leaking, incompatible, or difficult to waterproof confidently. Keep the surround only when it is sound, dry, compatible, and worth preserving. Have the contractor explain what will be opened and how the wet area will be protected.
